title: 1957 AHSME Problem 12
statement: Comparing the numbers \(10^{-49}\) and \(2\cdot10^{-50},\) we may say:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: the first exceeds the second by \(8\cdot10^{-1}\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the first exceeds the second by \(2\cdot10^{-1}\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
the first exceeds the second by
\(8\cdot10^{-50}\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the second is five times the first

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the first exceeds the second by \(5\)

solutions.text:
Using a common power of ten, \[ \begin{gathered} 10^{-49}-2\cdot10^{-50}\\ =(10-2)10^{-50}\\ =8\cdot10^{-50}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Express both numbers with the same power of ten
